name: Positive 4-3-1-2 Narrow

slots.why: Distributes short to the midfield triangle.
Attacking full-back on the left supplies the team's width and overlaps on that side.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate.
Ball-playing defender starts moves from the back.
Support full-back on the right stays more conservative, so the team has one attacking flank and one safe one.
Defensive central midfielder screens the defence and allows the others to go forward.
Deep-lying playmaker sets the tempo and keeps the ball moving.
Box-to-box midfielder joins the attack and supports the press.
Advanced playmaker is the creative centre of the team and feeds both strikers.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) links the playmaker to the other striker.
Advanced Forward runs in behind. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A narrow 4-3-1-2 using three central midfielders and an advanced playmaker behind two complementary forwards.
whyGood: It overloads central zones while the wing-backs provide the width that the midfield shape lacks.
whyThisShape: A narrow 4-3-1-2: three central midfielders and an attacking midfielder behind two strikers, so five players work in the centre. The full-backs provide all of the width, and the midfield can overload the middle and keep the ball.
whenToUse: When your best players are central and you lack wingers, or against a team with only two central midfielders that you can outnumber.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that attack the flanks, since your full-backs are the only wide players and will be stretched.

instructionRationale.Fairly Narrow: Keep the central combinations close; the selected wide defenders supply the outside outlets.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Work Ball Into Box: Look for an opening around the penalty area rather than encouraging speculative shots.
instructionRationale.Overlap Left: Ask the left-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Overlap Right: Ask the right-sided receiver to consider the outside run; this requires a wide defender who can supply that run.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: Defend from a middle block; the forward roles still determine which players challenge the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Full Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
